subject: botany
question_text: Name the books written by Parasara and mention the important aspects discussed in those books.

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Krishiparasaram
lines: a) Krishiparasaram — in it Parasara described
agriculture and also wrote about weeds.
It is the oldest book on agriculture.
steps.why: One mark per book, and each book needs its aspects: Krishiparasaram covers agriculture and weeds, and its status as the oldest book on agriculture is the marked detail.
common_mistakes: Naming the book without its contents — the question asks for the aspects discussed.
Dropping the 'oldest book on agriculture' line — that status is part of the expected answer.
steps.memory_tip: Krishi means farming — Krishiparasaram is Parasara's farming book, the oldest one on agriculture.
steps.margin_note: Two or three lines per book, contents included.

steps.label: Vrikshayurveda
lines: b) Vrikshayurveda — in it he described the
types of forests and the external and
steps.why: The second book carries its own aspects: forest types and the external and internal characters of plants — an early Indian record of plant morphology.
common_mistakes: Attributing Vrikshayurveda to another author — both books here are Parasara's.
Writing 'about trees' alone — the book covers forests and plant characters, not trees only.
steps.memory_tip: Vriksha means tree — Vrikshayurveda is the tree-and-forest book; Krishiparasaram is the farm book.
steps.margin_note: Finish with the boxed line naming both books together.

insider_note: 'Name ... and mention ...' is a double instruction; a bare list of the two titles earns only half the marks.
